tagline: Along four waters, from the Ohio line to the St. Lawrence.
intro: From the Ohio line the trail takes Route 5 across Pennsylvania beside Lake Erie, within 2,000 feet of the water at Lake City, and carries on into New York through Dunkirk and Buffalo. There it turns north along the Niagara River, past the falls, then east along Lake Ontario through Rochester and Oswego.

At Cape Vincent the lake gives way to the St. Lawrence, and the road follows the river through the Thousand Islands past Massena to the Seaway International Bridge, 518 miles on. It was conceived in 1978 as an 80-mile stretch among the islands and worked its way west from there.

moments.title: Presque Isle
moments.text: A sandy peninsula arching out into Lake Erie, the base for Commodore Perry's fleet in the War of 1812 and still being reshaped by wind and waves.

moments.title: Lewiston
moments.text: Niagara Falls started here, at the escarpment. Over some 12,500 years it has worn its way nearly seven miles upriver, leaving the gorge behind it.

moments.title: Sackets Harbor
moments.text: In the fall of 1814 the Navy's shipyard made this Lake Ontario village the third-largest place in New York. It now keeps about 1,350 people and the Seaway Trail's headquarters.
